full_judgment: 27. From the evidence discussed above, it is found that P.W. 1 informant Monowara Begum, P.W. 2 Zahir Uddin and P.W. 3 Taslima Khatoon are witnesses to the occurrence. From the F.I.R. Ext. it is found that informant Mrs. Monowara Begum did not disclose the means of recognition of the accused persons. Since the alleged occurrence took place at about 9.00 P.M. on 28.5.08, the means of recognition is a matter of profound importance for proving the correct identity of the accused persons. Although accused Shahadat is known to the witnesses, yet in the back-drop of very strained relation between the complainant party and he accused appellant. aggravated by a series Or civil and criminal litigations, the importance of correct and unfailing recognition of the accused can hardly be exaggerated. In this case, the prosecution led no evidence to dispel the lurking suspicion about the recognition of the accused persons. The deficiency of the prosecution is nil her magnified by the fact that it has failed to produce before the court, without any explanation any alamat of the means of recognition of the miscreants. The prosecution case has been disbelieved by the learned Special Tribunal in respect of the three co-accused and as such the conviction of the appellant On the basis of the suit-same evidence demands corroboration from snow independent sources. Although there are many houses around the place of occurrence, including a tea slot not even a single neighbouring person has been examined by the prosecution and no explanation has been furnished by I he prosecution for not examining the independent natural and probable wit-nesses. In the facts of the case, the defence can legitimately call upon the court to draw an adverse presumption against the prosecution under Section t 14(g) of the evidence Act.
